attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, giving his own verdict on the reported deal.

semantics.note: 'God no' is an unhedged, categorical denial that any of the described arrangement would happen, so it is a scored forecast. The normalised wording catches the scope (the deal plus the IPO step) and correctly gives no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'any of this' as failing if the core lease plus NVIDIA backing is signed is a fair, ordinary reading of a categorical 'any'. Not requiring the July dollar figures is reasonable. The result does turn on the scope of 'this'.

evidence.note: A Reuters wire report dated 2026-08-17: NVIDIA agreed to guarantee up to $105B of lease payments for OpenAI's SB Energy Ohio campus under a 20-year lease. This meets the early-contradiction rule.
A trade report dated 2026-08-18 confirming OpenAI signed a 20-year lease at the NVIDIA-backed SB Energy PORTS-Pike campus.

SoftBank's own disclosure that SB Energy filed an S-1 on 2026-09-01. The excerpt does not show the IPO rests on the OpenAI contract, and the IPO was not completed. Corroborating context only; not needed for the result.
A July 27 report showing the deal was still only in talks when he wrote. This is background to the claim, not the outcome.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, but the early-contradiction rule was met before the evaluation date. On 2026-08-17, Reuters and a trade report said OpenAI signed a 20-year lease at SB Energy's Ohio campus, with NVIDIA guaranteeing up to $105B of lease payments. The build-out and the $350B chip financing are unconfirmed, and the IPO was filed but not completed. Even so, the categorical 'any of this' denial fails.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will ... by the end of the year' with an over-$1.5T threshold. The year-end horizon and the threshold are kept. The revenue clause describes the state at the time he wrote.

contract.note: Counting reported capex from 2023 on plus stakes in AI labs is a fair, ordinary reading. The start date and which companies count are not stated, so the result depends on the evaluator's interpretation.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2026-12-31, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. The packet holds no evidence items: only guidance figures were looked at and not used. Nothing shows the early-support rule was met, so the forecast is not yet due and cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words. He relies on SemiAnalysis figures but asserts them himself.

semantics.note: Present-tense factual claim about $200 plans allowing $8K–$14K of monthly usage. 'Not a business model' is opinion and is correctly left ungraded by the contract.

contract.note: Valuing 'burn' at API list prices matches the measurement he relied on and is an ordinary reading. The June 1 to July 28, 2026 target period is reasonable for a present-tense statement.

evidence.note: SemiAnalysis's own post (Aug 23) says its June test found up to $8K a month (Anthropic) and $14K a month (OpenAI) from $200 plans. The test falls inside the target period.
A secondary summary dated June 16 reporting the same figures as API-equivalent token value from SemiAnalysis stress tests.
The caveat that the figures are API-list value, not the labs' actual compute cost. It qualifies 'burn' but does not change the dollar range.

reviews.rationale: SemiAnalysis's independent June 2026 test, in its own post and in a summary published before the article, found maxed-out $200 plans yield up to $8K a month at Anthropic and $14K at OpenAI, valued at API prices. That matches his range. Lower measurements fall outside the target period and are not in the packet. The 'not a business model' part is opinion and is not scored.
